dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Hello, and welcome to Svetloledovka. Feel free to ask me any questions you have. I'll do my best to answer them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Svetloledovka...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: As you can see, this is just a remote little town that makes its living from ice mining.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: If you're looking to earn some extra Mora with odd jobs, you can speak with Supervisor Sobolev. But if you're thinking of taking up ice mining long-term, you'll probably need to ask Pashkov first.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please excuse the interruption.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Not at all. It's part of the job. Oh, and be sure to keep warm. Don't stay outside too long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Sobolev...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Him? Well, to be honest, his duties cover all sorts of things. You can just think of him as the "General Manager" in charge of us workers.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: After all, everything from paying wages to fixing equipment has to go through him. That means he's always short-handed, and he often needs people to help out with odd jobs.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About Pashkov...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: He's our new safety officer. According to the rules, any prospective ice miner must pass the Safety Code exam before getting permission to enter the worksite.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Oh, and don't say I didn't warn you. This new safety officer is stubborn as a mule. Reasoning won't work on him, and neither will pressure. For all I know, he might be cracked in the head, so whatever you do, don't provoke him.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: I really don't get it. Why would he give up a nice, comfortable life at the troupe just to come suffer in a backwater like this...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About wages...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: I don't know what odd jobs pay. You'll have to ask Sobolev yourself about that. As for ice miners, we're paid by the piece here. Once you meet your quota, the more you do, the more you earn.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Night shifts also come with extra pay. That said, the ice pits are frighteningly cold at night... Unless you're really short on money, I generally wouldn't recommend it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Equipment repairs?

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: That would be the huge ice-mining machine in town. I heard it was brought in from the Energy Commission. No idea what's wrong with it, but it breaks down all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: We rough fellows can't make heads or tails of complicated machines, so the whole mess of managing that hunk of metal ended up falling on Sobolev.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: And, because of that machine, some rumors have started going around town. A while back, it even drew in a reporter, saying they wanted to investigate some kind of corruption...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Ah! I'm not saying I believe those rumors! No, no, what I mean is, there shouldn't be any rumors like that in the first place!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About what's happening up on the snowy mountain...

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Ah, you mean the rumors? You must be asking about the mansion up on the mountain. But it's not a rumor... it's actually out there.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: It belongs to Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess of the Snegoviks.... Though she rarely ventures out, she does occasionally invite humans to the manor as her guests.

dialogues.speaker: Nekrasov
dialogues.text: Mind you... word is that none of those guests ever make it back down.
